title: Ultramaster KR-106
short_description: The challenge for this round is to make a track using the Ultramaster KR-106 only.
long_description: The [Ultramaster KR-106](https://kayrock.org/kr106/) is an emulation of the famous Roland Juno 60 and 106 that was used by Enya and so many artists during the 80s and beyond.  Your challenge for this round is to **make a track using only the Ultramaster KR-106**.  You can use as many instances of the KR-106 as you wish, as well as any effect and any DAW as long as they are **free and open source**.  I forgot to add, you can also record your voice!  That way if you wish to layer hundreds of takes of your voice like Enya did, you can.  Now go compose something profound, but don't take two years like Enya, you have only a month and half!  *Happy music making!*

general: The challenge starts on the 1st of every odd month (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov) and ends on the 15th (excluded) of the follow month.
All submissions must be made with free (libre) software only.  This includes the DAW and all plugins.  A non-free operating system is allowed.
Submissions must be original work produced specifically for this context.  No covers, remakes, or remixes of existing work.
There is no song length limit.

Regardless of any challenge-specific restriction on plugins, basic utility plugins are always allowed, unless specified otherwise.  These include things like Limiter, EQ and Filtering, Volume and Pan, and MIDI manipulation.
Regardless of any software restriction, you are also allowed to use any hardware device to enhance your workflow, e.g. MIDI keyboard or other controllers.
submission: You must submit your entry before the 15th of the following month, i.e. at 11:59pm (UTC) the lastest on the 14th.
To submit you must post a link of your entry to the thread corresponding to the current round on the Linux Musicians forum.
voting: Voting runs from the 15th to the end of the following month of the challenge.  Failure to vote in time will result in disqualification.
Voting is done by ranking 5 submissions (excluding yours) from 1st (best) to 5th (worse among the 5 best).
Participants of previous challenges are also welcome to vote, even if they have not made a submission.

5 points are attributed to the submission with the highest rank, 4 to the second, 3 to the third, 2 to the fourth and 1 to the fifth.  No points are attributed to submissions that have not been ranked.
The submission with the most points wins.  In case of ties all submissions with the maximum number of points are winners.
Dependening on the round the winner(s) may receive prize(s) such as AUDIO tokens.
To vote, post a message with your ranking to the corresponding thread on the Linux Musicians forum, or send it as private message to one of the organizers of the challenge.
